title: Reflection on the Use of GenAI
text:
For this assessment, I primarily used Claude (by Anthropic) as my GenAI assistant. I chose Claude because:

It’s specifically designed for coding and technical tasks
Provides detailed, step-by-step explanations
Offers contextual understanding of web development and Quarto
Available through my university resources

I also occasionally referenced ChatGPT for comparison and alternative perspectives on certain technical challenges.



1. Setting Up the Quarto Website
When I first started, I was unfamiliar with Quarto’s syntax and structure. Claude helped me: - Understand the purpose of _quarto.yml configuration file - Learn proper YAML indentation (which caused me initial errors!) - Set up the correct output-dir: docs for GitHub Pages deployment
Example: When my navigation bar displayed raw YAML text instead of working links, Claude identified the formatting issue and provided a corrected structure with proper indentation.
2. Markdown Formatting and Syntax
GenAI was invaluable for learning Markdown quickly: - How to embed images: ![alt text](path/to/image.png) - Creating headers, lists, and emphasis - Troubleshooting image path issues (like when I used photo.jpg but the file was actually photo.jpg.png)
3. Git Version Control Guidance
One of my biggest challenges was understanding the Git workflow. Claude helped me: - Understand the difference between local rendering (localhost) and the live GitHub Pages site - Learn the commit-push cycle: git add → git commit → git push - Troubleshoot why my changes appeared locally but not on the live website
Example: When I asked “why after committing I don’t see anything in my git”, Claude explained that an empty Git tab means everything is committed successfully - this was actually correct behavior, not an error!
4. Content Structure and Organization
For the data visualization page, I showed Claude my Intermodal Transfer Analysis dashboard, and it helped me: - Structure the content with proper sections (What, Why, How) - Articulate the technical implementation details - Frame the story and insights in a clear, professional manner



Immediate, Personalized Learning - Unlike searching through documentation, GenAI provided answers specific to my exact problem - Explanations were tailored to my level of understanding - Available 24/7 when I worked on assignments late at night
Error Diagnosis and Debugging - When things didn’t work, I could paste screenshots or error messages - GenAI identified issues I wouldn’t have caught (like file extension mismatches) - Provided multiple solutions when one approach didn’t work
Learning Reinforcement - Each interaction taught me not just “how” but “why” - Built my confidence to experiment and try new approaches - Reduced frustration that often comes with learning new tools
Professional Writing Support - Helped structure technical explanations clearly - Suggested ways to present my work professionally - Improved the overall quality of my portfolio content



1. Over-Reliance Risk
Initially, I found myself asking GenAI for everything without trying first. I realized this wasn’t helping me learn deeply. I had to consciously: - Attempt problems myself before asking for help - Use GenAI for guidance rather than complete solutions - Verify information rather than blindly accepting it
2. Context Limitations
Sometimes GenAI didn’t have full context of my specific setup: - Assumed certain files existed when they didn’t - Couldn’t see my actual file structure without me describing it - Required multiple clarifying questions to understand my exact situation
3. Version-Specific Information
GenAI’s knowledge has a cutoff date, so: - Some Quarto features might be newer than its training data - I still needed to check official documentation for the latest syntax - Plugin compatibility information required verification
4. Critical Thinking Still Required
GenAI provided suggestions, but I had to: - Evaluate which solution best fit my needs - Understand the implications of different approaches - Make final decisions about design and content

title: Data Visualization
text:
Intermodal Transfer Analysis Dashboard




This interactive dashboard analyzes the integration between Singapore’s MRT (Mass Rapid Transit) and bus network systems. The visualization displays:

Geographic data: Interactive map showing the spatial distribution of bus stops around a selected MRT station
Key metrics displayed:

Number of bus stops within a specified search radius (16 stops)
Number of unique bus services available (50 services)
Search radius parameter (adjustable from 200m to 1000m, currently set at 550m)

Visual elements:

Blue markers representing individual bus stops
Red marker indicating the selected MRT station (Ang Mo Kio MRT)
Red circle showing the search radius coverage area
Base map with street-level detail for context





Context: This project was developed as part of my coursework in Data Engineering & Visualization at Singapore Institute of Technology, where we explored Singapore’s public transport connectivity and accessibility.
Objective: To assess the first-mile/last-mile connectivity of Singapore’s public transport system by measuring how well bus services support MRT stations. This analysis helps identify: - Areas with strong intermodal integration - Potential gaps in feeder bus coverage - Optimal transfer points for commuters
Problem Statement: Commuters often need to use multiple transport modes to complete their journeys. Understanding the density and variety of bus services around MRT stations is crucial for: - Urban transport planning - Evaluating accessibility for residents - Optimizing feeder bus routes



I chose this combination of interactive map and summary metrics because:

Geographic context is essential: Transport connectivity is inherently spatial - showing the physical distribution of bus stops reveals coverage patterns that numbers alone cannot convey
Interactive exploration: The dropdown selector and adjustable search radius allow users to:

Compare different MRT stations
Test various walking distance assumptions (200m to 1km)
Discover localized patterns specific to each neighborhood

Quantitative metrics provide clarity: The key performance indicators (16 bus stops, 50 unique services) give immediate numerical context to the visual patterns
Layered information hierarchy: The design presents information in progressive detail:

High-level summary cards for quick insights
Map visualization for spatial understanding
Individual markers for granular exploration





Data Sources: - LTA DataMall API: Real-time bus stop locations and service information - OneMap API: MRT station coordinates - OpenStreetMap: Base map tiles
Tools & Technologies: - Python: Data processing and API integration - Pandas: Data manipulation and cleaning - Folium/Leaflet.js: Interactive map visualization - Streamlit/Dash: Web application framework (if applicable) - Geopy: Geospatial distance calculations
Key Technical Challenges: - Handling large datasets (thousands of bus stops across Singapore) - Calculating accurate geodesic distances on Earth’s curved surface - Optimizing map rendering performance for smooth user interaction - Ensuring data accuracy and real-time synchronization with LTA systems



From analyzing multiple MRT stations:

Central stations have higher coverage: Stations in mature estates like Ang Mo Kio, Bishan, and Tampines show 40-60 unique bus services within 550m
Search radius impact: Increasing the search radius from 200m to 550m typically doubles the number of accessible bus services, but beyond 800m, the rate of increase slows significantly
Network hub identification: Certain stations (like Ang Mo Kio in this example) serve as major interchange points with extensive feeder networks
Coverage disparities: Newer MRT stations in developing areas may have fewer bus connections, highlighting areas for transport planning attention




This analysis framework can be used for: - Transport planning: Identifying areas requiring additional feeder bus services - Property development: Assessing transport connectivity for new residential projects - Commuter apps: Helping users find optimal transfer points - Research: Studying the evolution of Singapore’s integrated transport network



This project taught me the importance of combining multiple visualization techniques - quantitative metrics, geographic representation, and interactive elements - to tell a complete story. The key learning was that effective data visualization isn’t just about displaying data; it’s about enabling users to explore and derive their own insights.
The interactive nature of this dashboard allows different stakeholders (urban planners, researchers, commuters) to use the same tool for different purposes, demonstrating the power of flexible, user-driven visualization design.

This visualization was created as part of my Data Engineering & Visualization coursework, demonstrating the application of geospatial analysis and interactive dashboard design to real-world urban transport challenges.

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text: During my diploma studies at Temasek Polytechnic, I developed an automated data extraction and processing workflow for an ESG (Environmental, Social, and Governance) compliance platform using UiPath and Alteryx.*

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Background and Motivation
Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting has become increasingly critical for organizations to demonstrate their commitment to sustainable practices. However, ESG data collection is often: - Manual and time-consuming: Extracting data from multiple sources and formats - Error-prone: Human data entry mistakes affecting accuracy - Inconsistent: Different data formats across various reporting systems - Resource-intensive: Taking up valuable analyst time that could be spent on insights

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Project Objectives
The primary goal was to streamline ESG data management by:

Automating data extraction from multiple sources (Excel spreadsheets, PDFs, web portals)
Standardizing data formats across different reporting frameworks (GRI, SASB, TCFD)
Validating data quality with automated error checking and flagging
Reducing processing time from days to hours
Improving accuracy by minimizing manual data entry

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Technologies and Tools Used

Core Technologies

UiPath: Robotic Process Automation (RPA) platform for workflow automation
Alteryx: Data preparation and blending tool for ETL processes
Python: Custom scripting for data validation and transformation
Power BI: Dashboard creation for data visualization and insights
Microsoft Excel: Data source and validation interface



Technical Architecture
Data Sources → UiPath (Extraction) → Alteryx (Transformation) → Database → Power BI (Visualization)

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Key Features Implemented

1. Automated Data Extraction

Built UiPath robots to extract data from:

PDF sustainability reports
Excel templates from different departments
Web-based ESG disclosure platforms
Email attachments from stakeholders




2. Data Transformation Pipeline

Created Alteryx workflows to:

Standardize different date formats (DD/MM/YYYY, MM-DD-YY, etc.)
Convert units (metric tons to kg, kWh to MWh)
Map data to appropriate ESG frameworks
Handle missing or incomplete data




3. Quality Assurance Checks

Implemented validation rules:

Numeric range checks (e.g., energy consumption within expected bounds)
Completeness verification (all required fields populated)
Cross-referencing with previous period data for anomaly detection
Duplicate entry identification




4. Error Handling and Logging

Built robust error management:

Exception handling for missing files or inaccessible sources
Detailed logging of all automation steps
Email notifications for critical failures
Manual intervention queue for complex cases

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Challenges and Solutions

Challenge 1: Inconsistent Data Formats
Problem: Different departments submitted ESG data in varying formats, making standardization difficult.
Solution: - Created comprehensive data mapping templates - Developed Alteryx workflows with dynamic field recognition - Implemented fuzzy matching for similar-but-not-identical field names - Built validation layer to flag non-standard formats for manual review


Challenge 2: PDF Data Extraction Accuracy
Problem: UiPath’s OCR struggled with scanned PDFs and complex table layouts.
Solution: - Implemented multiple extraction strategies (native PDF reading vs. OCR) - Used anchor-based extraction for structured tables - Added post-extraction validation by cross-checking totals - Created manual review process for low-confidence extractions


Challenge 3: System Integration
Problem: Connecting UiPath, Alteryx, and the company’s database systems securely.
Solution: - Used API connections where available - Implemented secure file transfer protocols - Created intermediate staging database for data handoffs - Established clear data governance and access controls

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Results and Impact

Quantifiable Achievements

80% reduction in processing time: What took 2-3 days now completes in 4-6 hours
95%+ accuracy rate: Automated validation reduced data entry errors significantly
500+ hours saved annually: Freed analysts to focus on insights rather than data collection
Scalability: System handles 3x more data sources without additional staff



Qualitative Benefits

Improved data quality: Consistent formatting and validation rules
Faster reporting cycles: Ability to generate ESG reports on-demand
Better audit trail: Complete logging of data lineage and transformations
Enhanced stakeholder confidence: More reliable and timely ESG disclosures

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Technical Learning Outcomes

Skills Developed

RPA Development: Mastered UiPath Studio, including:

Sequence and flowchart design
Exception handling and logging
Orchestrator deployment and monitoring

ETL Pipeline Design: Gained expertise in:

Data extraction from diverse sources
Complex transformation logic
Load optimization strategies

Process Analysis: Learned to:

Map current-state business processes
Identify automation opportunities
Design future-state optimized workflows

Project Management: Experienced:

Stakeholder communication and requirements gathering
Agile development methodology
Testing and UAT coordination




Professional Growth
This project taught me valuable lessons about: - The importance of thorough documentation - Balancing automation with human oversight - Managing stakeholder expectations - Iterative development and continuous improvement

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Real-World Application
The skills and knowledge gained from this project directly apply to:

Fintech compliance: Automating regulatory reporting for financial institutions
Data analytics: Building robust data pipelines for analytical workloads
Business process optimization: Identifying and automating repetitive tasks
ESG technology: Contributing to the growing field of sustainability technology

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Future Enhancements
If I were to continue this project, I would explore:

Machine Learning Integration: Use ML to predict missing data points based on historical patterns
Natural Language Processing: Extract ESG metrics from unstructured text in reports
Real-time Monitoring: Implement continuous data feeds rather than batch processing
Blockchain for Transparency: Use distributed ledger for immutable ESG data records

title: Capstone Project: ESG Data Automation Platform
text:
Reflection
This capstone project was instrumental in shaping my career path toward fintech and data analytics. It demonstrated how technology can transform traditional business processes and create measurable value.
The experience of working with real stakeholders, managing real data, and delivering real business impact was invaluable. It prepared me for the challenges of professional data analytics work and reinforced my passion for using technology to solve practical business problems.
Most importantly, it taught me that successful automation isn’t just about technology - it’s about understanding the business context, working with people, and continuously improving based on feedback.

This project was completed during my internship at KPMG Singapore as part of my Diploma in Accountancy and Finance at Temasek Polytechnic. It represents the culmination of my accounting background, technical skills development, and interest in process automation.
